Looking at this systematically, I need to estimate how often each app gets named across 100 diverse queries. Let me categorize and work through them.

**Key observations from the query mix:**

- ~35 are generic "best/recommended meditation app" queries (by platform, audience, or use case) → all three apps commonly named
- ~6 are Meta Quest/Oculus VR queries → Headspace XR dominates; Calm and IT essentially absent
- 2 are "orange branding" queries → Headspace (orange dot logo)
- 1 is NHS staff → Headspace had that partnership
- 3 are Garmin queries → niche; none of the three has strong Garmin integration
- 2 are "calm alternative words/songs" → about the English word, not the app; apps rarely named
- 1 is "meditation without app" → about not using apps at all
- ~8 are "free/no subscription" queries → Insight Timer strongly boosted
- 4 are explicit-name queries (calm/headspace alternatives, "best meditation app calm/headspace") → the named app appears ~99%, alternatives also named
- Several very niche queries (IBS, labor, deaf, co-parenting, flashing lights) → specialized apps dominate, big three less likely

**Per-app reasoning:**

- **Insight Timer** (~50%): Dominates free/no-subscription queries and Buddhist/experienced meditator queries. Drops out entirely for VR, orange branding, word-synonym, and song queries. Less likely in many niche medical/demographic queries. Named less reflexively than Calm/Headspace in generic recommendations.

- **Calm** (~64%): Named in nearly all generic recommendation queries and sleep queries (where it's the standout). Appears in "alternative to Headspace" queries. Drops out of VR/Quest queries, orange branding, word-synonym queries, and NHS query. Slightly less dominant than Headspace in platform-specific and editorial-pick queries.

- **Headspace** (~72%): Highest overall because it captures everything Calm does in generic queries, PLUS dominates ~6 VR/Quest queries, 2 orange branding queries, the NHS query, and the Wirecutter/NYT queries. Also appears in all "Headspace alternative" queries by definition. Its only major absences are the word-synonym/song queries and "meditation without app."

```json
{"Insight Timer":50,"Calm":64,"Headspace":72}
```

Named rates averaged across the 100 queries: Calm appears most often, Headspace is frequently named in generic recommendations and its explicit alternative queries, and Insight Timer is a common free or practice focused recommendation. Explicit name queries count even when the app is criticized or compared.

{"Insight Timer":48,"Calm":57,"Headspace":55}

I'll work through all 70 queries, using the search results to calibrate regional availability, canonical recommendations, and feature fit.

**Key structural factors from research:**
- **YNAB** has the broadest international bank connectivity (US, Canada, UK, EU) and longest brand history. It appears in virtually every US-centric roundup and many international ones. It has a dedicated ADHD page, a student discount, and is the canonical zero-based budgeting pick.
- **Monarch Money** rose as the #1 Mint replacement. Strong for couples (unlimited collaborators). Expanded to Canada but otherwise US-focused. No free tier.
- **Rocket Money** is US-only (relies on Plaid). Has a free tier, making it appear in "free" queries. Known primarily for subscription tracking. Drops out of nearly all international queries.

**Query-by-query reasoning (grouped):**

- **Generic US "best budgeting app" queries** (~20 queries: 1, 6, 11, 15, 22, 24, 30, 32, 33, 36, 37, 45, 46, 53, 54, 55, 56, 67, 68, 70): All three appear in most canonical roundups. ~75-95% each.
- **Couples queries** (2, 18): Monarch near-certain (~95%), YNAB high (~82%), Rocket Money moderate (~39%).
- **Free-focused queries** (3, 47, 50, 63): Rocket Money's free tier gets it named (~72%). Monarch/YNAB are paid, mentioned as paid alternatives ~30% each.
- **No-subscription/no-bank-sync** (4, 5, 49): All three are subscription-based or known for bank sync. Low fit. ~12-20%.
- **"Alternative to X" queries** (7, 8, 51, 52): Named app ~98%. The other two named as alternatives ~40-82%.
- **"Like Mint" query** (27): Monarch is THE Mint replacement (~92%). YNAB/Rocket Money also commonly listed.
- **International queries where all three are weak** (9-Australia, 19-Germany, 21-HK, 23-India, 25-Kenya, 29-Malaysia, 35-Philippines, 39-SA): Local apps dominate. Monarch ~3-12%, YNAB ~8-30%, Rocket Money ~3-5%.
- **English-speaking international** (13-Canada, 31-NZ, 43/44-UK, 48-free UK, 57-Canada free, 69-Ireland): YNAB ~30-48%, Monarch ~15-65%, Rocket Money ~5-20%.
- **Europe queries** (16, 17, 61, 62): YNAB has EU connections (~42-45%). Monarch ~20-22%. Rocket Money ~5-8%.
- **Niche audience** (26-kids, 42-teens): Dominated by Greenlight/GoHenry. All three ~8-15%.
- **ADHD query** (10): YNAB has dedicated page (~70%). Others lower.
- **Grocery-specific** (20, 65): Likely about grocery deal apps. All three ~8-25%.
- **Debt/overspenders** (34, 41, 60): YNAB's methodology fits well (~68-75%). Others moderate.
- **Students** (40, 58): YNAB student discount gets it named (~60%). Rocket Money free tier helps (~42-45%).
- **Dave Ramsey** (14): EveryDollar dominates. YNAB mentioned for zero-based comparison (~65%).
- **Freelancers** (64): YNAB good for variable income (~60%). Monarch ~45%.
- **Linux/macbook/ipad** (28, 30, 70): Web-based apps. YNAB/Monarch have web apps. Reasonable mention rates.

**Averaged across all 70 queries:**
- Monarch Money: ~43%
- YNAB: ~52%
- Rocket Money: ~37%

```json
{"Monarch Money":43,"YNAB":52,"Rocket Money":37}
```

Regional queries make Rocket Money and Monarch Money less likely to appear, while YNAB is a plausible recommendation across more countries. The explicit “YNAB alternatives” and “Rocket Money alternative” queries also count the named app even when the answer discusses alternatives.

{"Monarch Money":30,"YNAB":43,"Rocket Money":25}

Now I have the key facts I need. Let me work through all 100 queries systematically.

**Key language coverage:**
- **Duolingo**: ~40+ languages including Arabic, Chinese, Dutch, French, German, Greek, Hawaiian, Hebrew, Hindi, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latin, Norwegian, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Vietnamese, Welsh, and more
- **Babbel**: 14 languages — Danish, Dutch, English, French, German, Indonesian, Italian, Norwegian, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish
- **Busuu**: 14 languages — Arabic, Chinese, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish, Turkish

**Reasoning by query category:**

**Generic "best app" queries (Q1, Q10, Q24, Q35, Q42, Q52, Q55, Q60, Q68, Q82):** Duolingo nearly always named (~95%). Babbel very frequently named as the top paid alternative (~85%). Busuu often but not always included (~55%).

**Free-focused queries (Q3, Q46, Q62, Q86, Q71, Q47, Q93, Q94):** Duolingo dominates as the free option (~95%). Babbel penalized as paid (~35%). Busuu mentioned for its free tier (~50%).

**"Alternatives to Duolingo" queries (Q7, Q11, Q17, Q26, Q30, Q54, Q58, Q73, Q78):** Duolingo always named (~97%). Babbel almost always named as top alternative (~87%). Busuu frequently named (~70%).

**Busuu-specific queries (Q8, Q51, Q98):** Busuu ~99%. Duolingo ~55-95%. Babbel ~20-55%.

**Language-specific queries where all three support the language** (Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish — Q15-16, Q18, Q20-21, Q25, Q34, Q36-38, Q63, Q81, Q85): All three commonly named; Duolingo ~90%, Babbel ~80%, Busuu ~55%.

**Language-specific queries Babbel doesn't support** (Arabic, Chinese/Mandarin, Japanese, Korean, Greek, Hebrew, Hindi — Q13, Q19, Q22-23, Q28, Q53, Q64-67, Q75, Q92, Q99): Babbel rarely named (~15%). Busuu named when it supports the language (~55% for Arabic/Chinese/Japanese/Korean, ~8% for Greek/Hebrew/Hindi).

**Language-specific queries neither Babbel nor Busuu support** (Bengali, Malayalam, Welsh, Latin, Irish, Thai, Ukrainian, Afrikaans, Urdu — Q12, Q27, Q29, Q43, Q45, Q69, Q77, Q87, Q89, Q91, Q100): Duolingo named ~40-88% (depending on whether Duolingo supports it). Babbel ~5-10%. Busuu ~5%.

**"No AI" queries (Q4, Q6, Q44, Q47, Q50, Q76, Q94):** Duolingo often named as the AI-heavy app to avoid (~65%). Babbel sometimes named as more traditional (~48%). Busuu ~30%.

**Niche/specific queries** (owl=Duolingo Q5/Q33, blue cat Q95, insults/roasts Q49/Q96, Netflix Q31, driving Q59, couples Q14, library card Q93): Duolingo dominates owl queries; others get very low scores for the truly niche ones.

**Kids queries (Q2, Q57, Q70, Q71):** Duolingo strong (~95%). Babbel weak (~25%). Busuu weak (~14%).

**Paid/offline/conversation/speaking (Q32, Q48, Q56, Q79, Q80, Q84):** Babbel often strong here (~80-85%).

After going through all 100 queries individually, computing per-query naming probabilities, and averaging:

- **Duolingo**: Very high baseline; penalized only on ~10 truly niche/off-target queries. Average ~83%.
- **Babbel**: Strong on generic, paid, conversational, Duolingo-alternative queries; weak on unsupported languages, kids, free, and niche queries. Average ~48%.
- **Busuu**: Similar pattern to Babbel but less consistently mentioned in generic queries; boosted by 3 Busuu-specific queries; weak on many unsupported languages and niche queries. Average ~41%.

Cross-check: Duolingo is named in almost all queries; Babbel in roughly half; Busuu in roughly 2 out of 5. These align with the question mix (many language-specific queries where smaller catalogs hurt Babbel/Busuu, several Duolingo-centric queries, and only 3 Busuu-specific queries).

```json
{"Babbel":48,"Duolingo":83,"Busuu":41}
```

The explicit Duolingo and Busuu queries make those names likely to appear, including in comparisons and alternatives. Across the many language-specific and use-case queries, Babbel and Busuu are more marginal mentions than Duolingo, so their estimates stay lower.

{"Babbel":34,"Duolingo":76,"Busuu":39}

## Reasoning

I searched to verify the relative prominence of each app in Korean budgeting app recommendation contexts. Key findings:

- **편한가계부** and **뱅크샐러드** are the two canonical Korean budgeting apps — they appear in virtually every recommendation article, blog roundup, and community discussion. They're the "default" pair the AI would surface on any generic or platform-specific recommendation query.
- **위플 가계부** is well-known (especially as an iOS staple, described as "iOS 1위" in some articles) but sits in a second tier. It appears in longer lists (TOP 5–6) and is more likely to be named in iPhone-specific or comparison queries, but gets dropped from shorter lists.

**Query-by-query logic (summarized):**

| Query type | 편한 | 뱅크 | 위플 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Generic recommendation (1,2,17,39) | ~93% | ~93% | ~58% | Both top-2 nearly guaranteed; 위플 in longer lists |
| Community-sourced rec (5,6,9,11,13,14,24) | ~82% | ~78% | ~48% | AI often falls back to known apps when community content is thin |
| Community general (3,10,12,19) | ~75% | ~72% | ~38% | Less recommendation-focused |
| Platform-specific Android (15,29,31) | ~93% | ~90% | ~40% | 위플 less associated with Android |
| Platform-specific iPhone/Apple (18,20,27,30) | ~88% | ~82% | ~72% | 위플's iOS prominence lifts it |
| Free/beginner/ranking (25,26,32,33,35) | ~90% | ~88% | ~55% | |
| Feature-specific (22,23,28,34,36,37) | ~68% | ~57% | ~38% | Varies by feature match |
| 만들기/디자인 (4,7,16) | ~17% | ~17% | ~10% | Not recommendation queries |
| 미국 (8,21) | ~21% | ~17% | ~11% | US-focused → US apps dominate |
| 비교 (38) | ~93% | ~93% | ~65% | |
| 뱅크샐러드 alternative (40,41) | ~87% | 100% | ~49% | 뱅크 in query; 편한 top alternative |
| 위플 alternative (42,43) | ~87% | ~81% | 100% | 위플 in query; both top alternatives |

Averaging across all 43 queries:

```json
{"편한가계부":76,"뱅크샐러드":73,"위플 가계부":48}
```
